p2: sqlite-transaction-state.ts:12-19 — If the probe ROLLBACK itself throws (e.g. SQLITE_BUSY while an empty deferred transaction is open), the helper leaks an open transaction on the caller's connection. The test file documents this failure mode; callsites either ignore rollback errors or propagate, but a leaked transaction from the *probe* (as opposed to caller's own) would block the same connection until closed. Consider documenting/wrapping so probe-owned state is always cleaned, or asserting the rollback target.

sqlite-transaction-state.ts:14-16 — Exact English error-message string match is version/locale fragile. Mitigated by the native boolean fast path (modern Node never reaches the probe) and by requiring code+errcode+message conjunction, so this is acceptable for the legacy-only path, but any Node 22.x patch release altering the message would turn a true 'active' result into a thrown error (fail-closed, not fail-open — hence P2 not P1).

kb-store-sqlite.ts:675-680 (withMutationTransaction) — The legacy probe introduces a BEGIN/ROLLBACK cycle before 'BEGIN IMMEDIATE', creating a small window where an external process could acquire the write lock; BEGIN IMMEDIATE then waits on busy_timeout or throws. Original native check had no such window. Behavior remains correct-by-timeout on the loop-owned connections where busy_timeout=5000 is set, but this is a subtle widening for standalone kb-store paths.

analysis_summary: The compatibility utility prefers the native boolean and falls back to a synchronous deferred BEGIN probe that returns true only on the exact nested-transaction error (code ERR_SQLITE_ERROR + errcode 1 + exact message) and rethrows everything else, so unrelated SQLITE_BUSY/locked/closed-connection failures cannot be misread as idle — matching the stated safety requirement of not relaxing to general SQLITE_ERROR. The probe is row-neutral (BEGIN deferred, immediate ROLLBACK) and savepoint-safe since an outer SAVEPOINT implies an open transaction, verified by the provided test design. All eight callsite replacements are semantically equivalent to the original isTransaction reads: mutation rollback guards retain outer-transaction detection, migration/ensureAssistantSource outer-transaction guards fail closed, and the metadata guard still rejects in-transaction observation. WithMutationTransaction nesting behavior is preserved. No authority-bypass, async-boundary, or hidden-writer changes are present in the diff.
